label: Evidence and gap map protocol
framework: Campbell-style evidence and gap map guidance

items.requirement: Identify the document as an evidence and gap map protocol.
items.prompt: What is the title and map scope for this evidence and gap map?
items.helpText: Signal the sector, population, intervention domain, and geographic or institutional scope.
items.exampleResponse: Evidence and gap map protocol: interventions to improve adolescent mental health outcomes in East Africa.

items.requirement: Explain the policy, practice, or research need for mapping evidence.
items.prompt: Why is an evidence and gap map needed, and who will use it?
items.helpText: EGMs are useful when users need to see evidence clusters and evidence gaps, not pooled effects.
items.exampleResponse: Decision-makers need a transparent map of where impact evaluations and systematic reviews exist before commissioning new studies.

items.requirement: Define the map framework and matrix dimensions.
items.prompt: What rows, columns, and filters will structure the map?
items.helpText: Common dimensions include intervention categories, outcome domains, population groups, geography, design, and confidence ratings.
items.exampleResponse: Rows will represent intervention categories; columns will represent mental health, education, safety, and service-use outcomes.

items.requirement: State the review objectives clearly and in alignment with the review type.
items.prompt: What are the primary and secondary objectives this protocol will guide?
items.helpText: Objectives should match the review type: estimate, map, explain, synthesize experiences, compare reviews, or maintain living evidence. State map objectives such as describing evidence clusters, identifying gaps, and supporting evidence commissioning.
items.exampleResponse: The primary objective is to synthesize the available evidence for the defined question. Secondary objectives include identifying gaps and describing implications for decision-makers.

items.requirement: Specify eligible evidence types and map boundaries.
items.prompt: Which study designs, systematic reviews, populations, contexts, interventions, and outcomes will be eligible?
items.helpText: State whether primary impact evaluations, process evaluations, systematic reviews, or other evidence types are included.
items.exampleResponse: We will include impact evaluations and systematic reviews of interventions targeting adolescents aged 10-19 in East Africa.

items.requirement: Describe comprehensive searches for published and grey literature.
items.prompt: Which databases, evidence portals, organizational repositories, registries, and websites will be searched?
items.helpText: EGMs usually require strong grey literature and organizational source coverage.
items.exampleResponse: We will search bibliographic databases, 3ie, Campbell, WHO, UNICEF, World Bank repositories, trial registries, and NGO websites.

items.requirement: Describe how searches will be developed, documented, and updated if needed.
items.prompt: How will the search strategy be constructed, peer reviewed, limited, documented, and updated?
items.helpText: Include core concepts, controlled vocabulary, limits, search dates, peer review, and supplementary search methods. Include grey literature, evidence portals, organisational repositories, and broad map-oriented search concepts.
items.exampleResponse: The strategy will combine topic concepts with appropriate subject headings, document all limits, and be adapted for each database.

items.prompt: How will records or sources be screened and selected, and how will disagreements or uncertainty be handled?
items.helpText: Specify screening stages, reviewer numbers, piloting or calibration, software, reasons for exclusion, and documentation. Describe screening for map eligibility and classification of evidence type.
items.exampleResponse: Screening criteria will be piloted. Records will be screened at title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved by discussion or a third reviewer.

items.requirement: Describe coding and data charting for the map.
items.prompt: What variables will be coded for each included record, and how will coding consistency be checked?
items.helpText: Include intervention, outcome, population, location, study design, status, and confidence fields.
items.exampleResponse: Two coders will pilot the codebook and chart intervention category, outcome domain, geography, design, sample, and review confidence rating.

items.requirement: State whether quality or confidence appraisal will be applied.
items.prompt: How will evidence quality, confidence, or review reliability be assessed and displayed?
items.helpText: Many EGMs appraise systematic review confidence and may classify primary study designs without full risk-of-bias assessment.
items.exampleResponse: Systematic reviews will be appraised using an adapted confidence checklist; primary studies will be coded by design and evaluation type.

items.requirement: Describe the planned synthesis, mapping, integration, or theory development approach.
items.prompt: How will the evidence be synthesized, mapped, integrated, or explained?
items.helpText: The method should fit the review type, data, and objective, and should specify how variation or heterogeneity will be handled. Describe the map matrix, gap interpretation, and visual or interactive outputs.
items.exampleResponse: Findings will be organized by the protocol framework and synthesized using methods appropriate to the available evidence and review objective.

items.requirement: Describe equity, context, subgroup, and applicability considerations.
items.prompt: Which equity, context, setting, population, implementation, or applicability factors must be captured in the protocol?
items.helpText: Consider geography, socioeconomic status, gender, age, disability, health system context, and implementation setting. Consider geography, socioeconomic status, gender, age, disability, health system context, and implementation setting.
items.exampleResponse: We will extract and report context and equity-relevant characteristics, including setting, population subgroup, implementation environment, and applicability considerations.

items.requirement: Describe stakeholder engagement in question refinement, interpretation, or dissemination.
items.prompt: Which stakeholders will be involved, at what stages, and how will their input influence the review?
items.helpText: Stakeholders may help refine questions, identify sources, interpret findings, or shape outputs. Explain how users will help validate map dimensions and interpret priority gaps.
items.exampleResponse: Stakeholders will be consulted during question refinement and interpretation of preliminary findings to improve relevance and usability.

items.prompt: What is the timeline for protocol finalization, searching, screening, extraction, appraisal, synthesis, review, and dissemination?
items.helpText: Include milestones, dependencies, review updates, and deadlines relevant to the review type. Include milestones, dependencies, review updates, and deadlines relevant to the review type.
items.exampleResponse: Protocol finalization will occur in month 1, searching and screening in months 2-3, extraction and appraisal in month 4, synthesis in month 5, and dissemination in month 6.

items.requirement: Define author, reviewer, advisor, and stakeholder responsibilities.
items.prompt: Who will be responsible for each stage of the review and how will conflicts or decisions be handled?
items.helpText: Include roles for search, screening, extraction, appraisal, synthesis, project management, decision escalation, and authorship. Include roles for search, screening, extraction, appraisal, synthesis, project management, decision escalation, and authorship.
items.exampleResponse: The information specialist will lead searches; two reviewers will screen and extract data; the methods lead will oversee synthesis and resolve methodological questions.

items.requirement: Describe map presentation, gap interpretation, and dissemination.
items.prompt: How will the interactive map, summary report, and gap interpretation be produced and shared?
items.helpText: Describe the map platform, evidence-gap categories, stakeholder review, and update plans.
items.exampleResponse: The final product will include an interactive matrix, downloadable dataset, technical report, and policy-facing evidence gap summary.

items.requirement: Identify appendices required for transparency and reproducibility.
items.prompt: Which appendices will be included to document methods and decisions?
items.helpText: Appendices may include search strategies, screening forms, extraction forms, appraisal tools, coding frameworks, stakeholder materials, and amendment logs. Include the codebook, map taxonomy, source list, and data dictionary.
items.exampleResponse: Appendices will include database search strategies, screening forms, extraction templates, appraisal tools, coding framework, and protocol amendments.
